title: probe
description: probe

title: Runtime prerequisites for the language front end
description: ADR 0011 needs three runtime features before the elaborator can describe real worlds: a change log, cell domains other than intervals, and phenomena that start and end. Each one is hard to add after content depends on its absence.
close_reason: All three runtime prerequisites are merged: the change log, set domains, and instances that start and end.

title: Language front end (ADR 0011)
description: The six stages of ADR 0011, the acceptance tests, and instantiation rules in source.

title: Measurement and verification
description: The research claims of Quadrilateral are measurements: cost, incrementality, determinism, explanation. These tasks give the project the instruments to make those measurements before the claims depend on them.

title: Level-of-detail research
description: Automatic model selection and the questions around it: uncertainty from abstraction, enclosure of detailed behavior by coarse predictions, and refinement triggered by broken assumptions (design sections 7 and 11.4; open questions 6, 8, 10).

title: Time, scheduling and coupling research
description: Temporal constraints, asynchronous clocks, implicit coupling and trajectory constraints (design sections 6.3, 10, 11.3; ADRs 0005, 0006, 0009 section 9).

title: Later research branches
description: Directions from the source conversation that no current work depends on (quadrilateral-review-fable.md section 8.2).

title: Change log for each boundary, and commit by changed cells
description: ADR 0011 section 6.6. Record (epoch, cell, old value, new value) for each replaced value and (epoch, cell, amount) for each stock change, in a defined order. Keep a list of changed cells so that commit does not scan every cell. Expose the log through the world API. The relation engine and a later differential engine read this log. Done when: a test checks the log of the two-room run against the state changes, and commit cost no longer grows with the number of unchanged cells.
close_reason: Completed: change log and commit by touched cells, merged in cf11888 (0bf5f9c). 6 changelog tests; 6 mutants caught; make test and make asan pass.

title: Cell domains other than quantity intervals
description: ADR 0011 consequences. State such as door: "open" | "closed" or a phase must be a cell. Add finite domains of atoms (a set of possible atoms that only narrows) and booleans to the network, with equality and membership propagators, without slowing interval cells. This is the CLP(X) pattern of design section 5. Write an ADR first: the representation and how kernels read and write such slots. Done when: a propagator over atoms passes the order-independence property test.
close_reason: Completed: set domains in the network (51b76a8) and in the world and kernel interface (this commit). ADR 0012 proposed. Order-independence and soundness properties cover mixed domains; 13 mutants caught after fixes; make test and make asan pass (77 tests).

title: Phenomena that start and end during a run
description: ADR 0011 section 7. A fire starts; it must become a phenomenon at a boundary. Write ADR 0013 first (ADR 0012 is finite-set domains): identity keys from the rule and the participants (never creation order), cells only ever added so indices stay stable, an ending instance transfers its stocks out first (as a model switch does), and its cells become dormant. Then implement create and end at boundaries in the world. Done when: a test starts and ends a phenomenon, conserves every stock exactly, and two runs give the same hash.
close_reason: ADR 0013 and its implementation are merged (b6d0bbd). tests/test_instances.c starts and ends an instance, conserves every stock exactly, and two runs give the same hash.

title: Front end stage 1: parser and syntax tree
description: ADR 0011 section 1. Lexer and parser for the CUE-like syntax, borrowed from Triangle parse.c under ADR 0003. Errors give file, line and column. Done when: Triangle's examples/workshop parses.
close_reason: The parser is merged to main (6eb065b). ADR 0014 is accepted. Triangle's workshop parses.

comments.author: chazu
comments.text:
State on 2026-11-21: the parser is implemented and committed on the branch quad-ijx.1. It is not merged and not pushed. 94 tests pass in the normal and sanitizer builds. Done-when is met: tests/data/workshop parses (45 declarations).

Pending decisions of the project owner:
1. ADR 0014 (docs/adr/0014-source-syntax.md) is 'proposed'. Accept it or correct it. Points to check: (a) 10m/x is one number with the unit m/x, so an author writes 10m / x. (b) 1e5 and 0x10 parse as numbers with the units e5 and x10, and stage 2 must reject them. (c) Five checks move to stage 2: literal conversion, unit names, function names, regular-expression patterns, attribute names. (d) Dropped from Triangle: ref(n), the file read of @embed, the clause prelude flag. (e) The parser replaces lets and adds a conjunct for each reference, as Triangle does. (f) The front end stops the process when memory runs out.
2. After ADR 0014 is accepted: merge quad-ijx.1 to main with a merge commit, push main, and close quad-ijx.1. Each needs the owner's word.
3. Then start quad-ijx.2 (type hierarchy and unifier, borrowed from Triangle types.c, fs.c, qc.c). Read the design document and the original chat before a design recommendation, and clarify questions first.

comments.author: chazu
comments.text:
Review of ADR 0014 on 2026-11-22. The user agreed to the attached unit syntax with these changes, which are in the working tree of the branch:
- An exact exponent form: 5.67e-8W/m^2/K^4. XNum.frac can be negative.
- The lexer rejects (, [ or a path directly after a compound unit (10m/sqrt(4)), with a hint about spaces.
- A syntax error at a name after a number with no unit (20 W/K) shows the attached form.
- ADR 0014: only a bare name joins a unit, and a reference is safe. The delimiter form 1000[J/K] is recorded as a future option.
- The stage 2 requirements are in a comment on quad-ijx.2.
The other points of ADR 0014 from the comment before this one still wait for the user's word. The status of the ADR is still proposed.

title: Front end stage 2: type hierarchy and unifier
description: ADR 0011 section 3 step 2. Borrow types.c (glb completion), fs.c (Tomabechi unification) and qc.c (quick check). Each unification has its own context. Literals with units convert exactly to quantity types (ADR 0001). Handle-based API, no text round trips. Done when: load results do not depend on file or declaration order (property test).
close_reason: Stage 2 is merged to main. ADR 0015 is accepted. The result of a load does not depend on the order of files or declarations (test_prop_load_order).

comments.author: chazu
comments.text:
Requirements from the review of ADR 0014 (unit syntax), for stage 2:
1. A let or a variable of a comprehension must not have the name of a unit symbol. Report an error at the binding. Reason: with a let s, 10m/s has two readings with the same dimension, and no other check finds the error (ADR 0014 section 2).
2. When a unit is unknown and its text contains / or *, the message must say that a bare name joined the unit, and that spaces around the operator make it arithmetic: 10m / x.
3. When a bare name is not found, it is a unit symbol, and it is the divisor of a plain number (0.1/s), the message must show the form 0.1s^-1.
4. Reject 0x10 (unit x10) as an unknown unit. The exponent form (1e-5) is now in the parser. A literal can have a negative count of fraction digits (1e5 has frac -5), and the conversion must handle it exactly.

comments.author: chazu
comments.text:
Decisions of the user on 2026-11-22, before the design:
- Scope: the core only. Comprehensions and built-in functions are quad-ijx.9, defaults and variants are quad-ijx.10, text constraints and interpolation are quad-ijx.11.
- ADR 0015 (docs/adr/0015-kinds-and-the-unifier.md) is written first. Its status is proposed, and no code starts before the user accepts it.
- A kind has the prefix %: %energy: { dimension: "J", scale: -3 }. The user proposed a prefix character, and % was the free one.

comments.author: chazu
comments.text:
State on 2026-11-22: stage 2 is implemented on the branch quad-ijx.2. It is not committed and not merged.
- ADR 0015 is accepted. Its consequences gained four findings from the implementation, and the sketch of ADR 0011 gained the supertype #Thermal, because a type introduces each feature once.
- New: src/front/kinds.c, types.c, fs.c, qc.c, resolve.c, xtree.c. Changed: parse.c (the %name token), util.c, front.h.
- Tests: tests/test_resolve.c with 10 tests, and the fixture tests/data/resolve. 105 tests pass in the normal build and with the address and thread sanitizers.
- Done when: met. 40 shuffled loads of the fixture give the same hash and the same text (test_prop_load_order).
- Mutation checks: 59 mutations of the new code. 57 are detected. 2 are equivalent (the choice of the scratch table, and one early return that a later check repeats).
- Limits: qf_build_text is for one thread at a time. Attributes are not in the content hash. Matching and the list of all conflicts are for stage 6.

comments.author: chazu
comments.text:
Decisions of the user on 2026-11-22 after the first implementation, all implemented and in ADR 0015:
- Each SI base dimension has a built-in kind (%length, %mass, %current, %temperature, %amount, %luminosity, with %time). One declaration can change the scale, conserved or the rounding of one of them. A second declaration is an error. %time, %count and %ratio are fixed.
- The angle is a built-in base dimension with the degree as its coherent unit: deg, turn, %angle. There is no radian.
- pct and ppm are unit symbols with no dimension. A unit symbol for a count (gp) waits for a need.
- A struct states its type: its place must already have the type that introduces its fields. Triangle's inference from the fields is gone. References through a field with no type stay.
- In the unit of a literal, a * after a / is an error: J/kg/K.
- Kept: a type introduces each feature once.
State: 107 tests pass in the normal build and with the address and thread sanitizers. 22 more mutations, all detected. Not committed, not merged.

title: Front end stage 3: prelude, elaborator, IR, and the two-room world
description: ADR 0011 sections 2 to 4. Prelude types, elaboration to an IR with a text form and the dependency graph, instantiation through the world API. Acceptance: the two-room world in source gives the same state hash at 1000 s as the C test build.
close_reason: Completed: the elaborator, the IR with its text form and dependency graph, and qi_instantiate (7b4a744). The two-room world in source gives the same state hash at 1000 s as the C build. ADR 0016 accepted. A law is a named field, and the prelude is in the package quad. make test and make asan pass (120 tests). Follow-ups: quad-ijx.12 and quad-ijx.13.

title: Front end stage 4: models, ports, interactions, reactions
description: ADR 0011 sections 4 and 5. Interactions lower to port connections and transfers; reactions to transfers with fixed ratios; models carry applicability, preserved information and cost. Acceptance: the phase 5 experiment in source reproduces the C results.

title: Front end stage 5: relations and the relation engine
description: ADR 0011 section 6. Datalog rules with set semantics, semi-naive evaluation, stratified negation and aggregation at boundaries, maintained from the change log. The compiler rejects cycles through negation. Done when: a reachability relation (which villagers can reach food) updates from the change log and matches a full recomputation.

title: Front end stage 6: runtime unification for agents
description: ADR 0007 and ADR 0011. Unification at run time on descriptions built from cells through handles, so agents can exchange partial descriptions (design section 13.4). Definite clauses as an explicit search facility at boundaries.

title: Instantiation rules in source
description: ADR 0011 section 7. Source declares when a phenomenon exists, for example combustion for each combustible above its ignition temperature. The rule runs at boundaries and creates or ends instances with stable keys.

title: Acceptance: port Triangle's workshop example
description: Design section 17.5. Port examples/workshop and measure how naturally the language expresses it, how much work is incremental, and which hot paths need native code. Write the findings down.

title: World snapshot and restore, with a mid-run replay test
description: ADR 0004 rule 8. Bruggadung never tested a save and restore in the middle of a run (its REVIEW.md 4.5). A snapshot holds the clock, the epoch, every cell, the active models, and each attachment's prediction, assumptions and event count (predictions decide boundaries, so they are state). Kernels with private state use save and restore. Done when: a run restored at 500 s and continued to 1000 s gives the same hash as an uninterrupted run, for the phase 4 and phase 5 worlds.
close_reason: Merged to main: qw_snapshot and qw_restore, with a replay test in the middle of a run for the worlds of phase 4 and phase 5.

title: Scale benchmark: many rooms, few changes
description: A generated world with thousands of rooms where few change at each boundary. Report boundaries, propagator runs, kernel advances and wall time. It is the baseline for incremental epochs and for the cost claims of level of detail.

title: EXPLAIN version 0: why this boundary, why this value, why this model
description: Design section 11.6. Record which attachment's horizon or event set each boundary, which propagator last narrowed each cell and from which inputs (with a version number for each cell, ADR 0007), and why each model is active. Report by feature path (ADR 0007). Done when: a query on the two-room run answers why the step is 5 s and why the temperature has its value.

title: Incremental epochs
description: ADR 0008. At a boundary, reset and run again only the propagators that a changed base can reach (start with the connected component), not the whole network. Decide in ADR 0004 which mode is the reference when a budget stops propagation early. Done when: the scale benchmark shows cost that grows with the change, and the results equal a full recomputation.

title: Coarse models publish bounded estimates at their ports
description: Design section 9.4 and 7.4. An aggregate room's mean temperature is not its boundary temperature; it must publish an interval with an error bound. Kernels must use the bounds soundly. The width of a port value is the uncertainty criterion of model selection.

title: Harness: does the coarse prediction enclose the detailed behavior?
description: Open question 8. Run coarse and detailed models side by side from the same state, and check and measure how often the coarse intervals enclose the detailed values.

title: Automatic model selection
description: Design section 7.1 and ADR 0010 section 4. Select the cheapest valid model at boundaries from observability (loci of focus), causal relevance, uncertainty, and budget, using qw_switch. A kernel that returns QK_INAPPLICABLE, or an input outside a valid range, requests a switch instead of stopping the run. Write an ADR first.

title: Scenario: an opened door invalidates a coarse fire
description: Open question 6 and design section 11.4. A coarse combustion model assumes oxygen within 5%; a door opens; the assumption breaks; selection refines the fire. Uses the existing assumption mechanism.

title: Refinement policies that produce plausible detail
description: Open question 10 and the owner's note on reification. Replace uniform noise with domain policies, for example a gradient from the boundary history, under the contract of ADR 0009 section 5. Consider retained latent state.

title: Predicted event windows as cells; reserve a backward-evaluation flag
description: Design sections 10.2 and 10.4, and review section 8.2. A kernel's predicted event window becomes a time cell that propagators can relate to other events. Also reserve a kernel flag for backward evaluation in kernel.h and ADR 0009, so evaluation directions stay visible. Small and cheap now.

title: Temporal constraints between events
description: Design section 10.4. Difference constraints between event cells (A before B, B within five minutes of A) narrow event windows forward and backward. The sum propagator with interval constants already expresses a difference constraint.

title: Asynchronous clocks for each phenomenon
description: ADR 0006. Conservative parallel discrete-event simulation with lookahead (Chandy, Misra, Bryant): each group advances to its own time where dependencies allow. The evaluator interface already permits it. Write an ADR first.

title: Model exchange: rate kernels solved as a group
description: ADR 0009 section 9. Kernels with QK_RATES report rates; the host solves tightly coupled groups together, for example with SUNDIALS CVODE. Compare with explicit coupling on the two-room analytic case.

title: Trajectory envelopes over a step
description: Open question 4. An evolution kernel publishes the range of a value over its step as an OUT interval, so that a propagator can check constraints such as 'never above this threshold during the interval'.

title: Probability distributions as values
description: Capability 4 of the first proposal, and predictions as 'a distribution over possible future events'. Decide a representation that keeps determinism and fits beside intervals.

title: Agents as actors, and subjective knowledge
description: Design sections 11.1 and 13.4. Agents with beliefs, goals and mailboxes whose decisions are proposals; knowledge separate from the authoritative simulation, as in Bruggadung.

title: Spatial state and a spatial index
description: The first architecture names spatial queries and sparse spatial updates. A Dwarf Fortress-like world needs them.

title: Differential evaluation of relations
description: Design section 15. Beyond semi-naive maintenance: differences indexed by (epoch, iteration), as Differential Dataflow does. Reads the change log.

title: Wrap an FMU as a kernel
description: Design section 15. FMI 3.0 interoperability through the ADR 0009 interface.

title: Narrowing kernels through ports that depend on a model
description: qw_attach refuses this today, because the watch list is fixed at attach. Register watchers again after a switch.

title: Index cell paths for lookup
description: qw_find is a linear search. Add an index that does not affect any iteration order (ADR 0004).

title: Front end: comprehensions and built-in functions
description: Split from quad-ijx.2 on 2026-11-22. Expand for and if comprehensions, computed labels, and built-in function calls when content loads. Borrow the comprehension part of Triangle's load.c and builtins.c (bruggadung f425574, ADR 0003). The result must not depend on file or declaration order. Done when: tests/data/workshop/data.tri loads with its comprehensions expanded.
close_reason: Merged to main: comprehensions, computed labels and 36 built-in functions, expanded when content loads.

title: Front end: defaults
description: Split from quad-ijx.2 on 2026-11-22. Resolve defaults (*v) after unification, as Triangle's resolve_defaults does: the more specific contributor wins, and a default that conflicts is dropped with a note. Not borrowed: @vary and random construction, until a design needs them (they must use the counter-based random numbers of ADR 0002). Done when: the defaults of the workshop example resolve as in Triangle.
close_reason: Merged to main: defaults resolve after unification with Triangle's rules. Variants of an instance are quad-u4c.

title: Front end: text constraints and interpolation
description: Split from quad-ijx.2 on 2026-11-22. Regular-expression constraints on text (=~, !~) with Triangle's regex.c and text.c, and string interpolation. The parser keeps the pattern as text (ADR 0014), so this issue adds the check of each pattern. Done when: tests/data/workshop/text.tri loads.
close_reason: Merged to main: text constraints with regular expressions, and interpolation when content loads.

title: Front end: intermediate cells for laws with nested expressions, literals and inequalities
description: Split from quad-ijx.3 on 2026-11-22 (ADR 0016). Stage 3 lowers a law of the form a == b or a == b op c, where a, b and c are references. A nested expression such as .power == .conductance * (.hot.temperature - .cold.temperature), a literal operand such as .t - 273.15K, and an inequality need more: an intermediate cell with an anonymous kind (ADR 0001) that is not authoritative state, a constant cell, and an inequality propagator. Decide if an intermediate cell has a path and if qw_hash covers it. Done when: the wall law of tests/data/resolve/physics.quad elaborates and narrows the power.
close_reason: Completed: a law can have inner expressions, numbers and inequalities. Inner values and numbers are derived cells, which are not state. ADR 0018 (proposed, for review). The wall law of tests/data/resolve/physics.quad elaborates and narrows the power. make test and make asan pass (125 tests).

title: Unrelated types can each have a field with the same name (reverse ADR 0015 section 5)
description: Decided by the project owner on 2026-11-22, after quad-ijx.3: the rule is a bad call in hindsight, and no good reason for it remains. Today a field name belongs to one type in a package. If #Wall declares hot, an unrelated type #RadiantWall cannot declare hot, and the author must write a common supertype. Since ADR 0016 a law is a named field, so two unrelated types also cannot each have a law named storage. The reason that ADR 0015 gave: with a generated supertype, one label could be a quantity in one type and text in another, with no message. Options to weigh in a new ADR that amends ADR 0015: (a) the compiler makes the common supertype itself, as its error message now tells the author to do, and the two declared types of the field must unify where one structure has both; (b) a feature belongs to each type that declares it (structural, as in CUE). Check what the borrowed type code assumes: feature numbering, appropriateness, feat_resolve, the quick check, and the package rule for features. Done when: two unrelated types in one package each declare hot: #ThermalPort and the content loads; two unrelated types each declare a law with the same name; a structure that gets one label with two types that do not unify gives an error at that place; the load-order property tests pass.
close_reason: Completed: unrelated types can each have a field with the same name. A feature has a list of introducing types, and the hierarchy gets no new type. ADR 0017 accepted, ADR 0015 and ADR 0016 amended. make test and make asan pass (122 tests).

title: Small examples and a command-line tool, to show the use of the language and to find rough edges
description: Requested by the project owner on 2026-11-22. A user has no way to run a .quad file: the front end is a library with tests. Add a small command-line tool (check, ir, run) and a directory of small examples. Write down each rough edge that an example shows, as an issue.
close_reason: The tool and the examples are on main. Each rough edge that the examples showed has its own issue: quad-rf3, quad-fjp and quad-znr are done; quad-shg, quad-u0g and quad-nu8 are open.

title: A stock gets its first value from the laws
description: Found with the examples (quad-0r7). A room needs energy: 3031500J, which the author computes by hand from 303.15 K and 10000 J/K. With temperature: 303.15K and no energy, the compile says: the stock r.energy needs an exact value. The laws give exactly one value. Proposal: when a stock has no exact value, propagate the laws once before the world is built, and take the value if it is a point. If it is a range, report the range. Needs a short ADR, because it changes ADR 0016 section 2.
close_reason: Merged to main: @derived fields and the start pass of the elaborator (ADR 0019)

title: Behavior over time in source: a rate law, with no C kernel
description: Found with the examples (quad-0r7). The only behavior over time is the native conduction kernel. A user cannot write a heater, a pump, a leak or growth. Every example of change is two rooms and a wall. This is the largest gap for showing the use of the language. Related: quad-ijx.4 (interactions and reactions), design section 12.4 (the path to self-hosting). A first form: a transfer between two stocks with a rate that a law gives.
close_reason: Merged to main: #Interaction with a rate and the kernel native.rate (ADR 0020). Follow-ups: quad-pr0, quad-iil.

title: Messages of the unifier in the words of the author
description: Found with the examples (quad-0r7). Examples: (1) voltage: 12A gives 'struct: conflict at voltage: %voltage vs dim[A] & 12'. Better: 12 A is not a %voltage (V). (2) t: 25C gives a conflict with dim[s A]: C is the coulomb. Add a hint for a temperature: write kelvin. (3) 'unknown feature volts': say field, and list the fields of the type. (4) mass: 0.0001g says 'not a whole number of quanta of the kind': say the smallest step of the kind and how to change the scale. (5) The prefixes 'struct:' and 'conjunction:' are words of the implementation.
close_reason: Merged to main: unifier messages name the field, the value with its unit, and the kind

title: A law that cannot hold stops the whole world
description: Found with the examples (quad-0r7). In load.quad, one phenomenon with a contradiction hides the values of every other phenomenon. The network has one contradiction flag. A contradiction could stay inside the connected component of its cells. Related: quad-5xe.4 (incremental epochs by component) and quad-5xe.3 (EXPLAIN): the tool now names the law and its values, as a first step.

title: Defaults for a kernel's settings, and less text for a port
description: Found with the examples (quad-0r7). (1) Each wall must set tolerance: 1pct, a setting of the kernel that a new user does not know. Defaults (quad-ijx.10) solve it: tolerance: *1pct. (2) A room writes its port field by field: west: #ThermalPort & { temperature: .temperature, capacity: .capacity, energy: .energy }. A shorter form for a port that is a view of the fields with the same names would help.
notes: 2026-11-24: part (1) is done with quad-ijx.10. The wall type of examples/thermal.quad states tolerance: *1pct | %ratio. Part (2), a shorter form for a port, stays open.

title: Display units and ranges of kinds
description: Found with the examples (quad-0r7). (1) A kind has no display unit: the tool has its own small table from dimension to unit (J, W, V). Temperatures are in kelvin only. (2) A mass or a count can be negative unless each field says >=0: order.crate_mass is <= 24.375 kg with no lower bound. A kind could declare a range. (3) The tool prints time in seconds only.

title: A scale that follows the value, for derived cells
description: From the review of ADR 0018 on 2026-11-22. A derived cell has a fixed scale with limits: at most 12 decimals, and for a quotient at least 6 decimals more than the default of its dimension. This serves common magnitudes. It does not serve a very small or a very large inner value: h * f with the Planck constant is 3e-19 J, which is below 10^-12. A derived cell is not state, so it can have another domain: an interval with a decimal exponent that follows the value, with integer arithmetic and outward rounding (deterministic, sound). ADR 0012 added set cells as a second domain in the same way. Until then, the author gives such a value a field with a kind.

title: Variants of an instance: alternatives of structures in an instance
description: Split from quad-ijx.10 on 2026-11-24. ADR 0015 named defaults and variants together. Defaults are done. In Triangle, an instance with alternatives of structures has one version for each combination, and construction draws one (with @vary and a seed). A phenomenon of a world has one structure, so today such an instance is an error: the message tells the author to give the alternatives to a type. Decide first if a world needs variants at all. If yes, the draw must use the counter-based random numbers of ADR 0002.

title: An expression as the value of a field
description: Found with ADR 0020 (quad-znr). A computed field takes two lines today: a field with a dimension, and a law. Example: outflow: %volume / %time, and speed: .outflow == .volume / .empties. With an interaction, one flow takes three lines. Fix: an expression as the value of a field, as in rate: .volume / .empties. The elaborator changes it into a field with the dimension of the expression and a law. This helps each computed field, not only a rate. It needs a decision on the name of the law and on @derived for such a field.

title: A rate for a state field of a kind that is not conserved
description: Found with ADR 0020 (quad-znr). Only a stock can change through an interaction. A position that follows a speed must have a kind with conserved: true, and an interaction with conserved: false. The word conserved reads wrong there: the kind flag means that only a transfer changes the value. Fix options: a rate for a state field of a kind that is not conserved (the kernel role QK_STATE), or another word for the kind flag. Decide with quad-ijx.4.

title: Stage 4A: models, ports and maps in source, with qi_switch
description: ADR 0021 sections 1 to 5 (first part) and 8. A model is a field below #Model. The phenomenon names the model at the start. A port of the phenomenon is the port of the active model. A map is a field below #Map. qi_switch finds the map. Acceptance tests 1 and 2 of ADR 0021.

title: Stage 4B: an interaction with no rate states a transfer of the kernel
description: ADR 0021 section 6. The compiler checks each interaction with no rate against the contract of the kernel. Inspection shows each transfer of the contract, also one that source does not state. Acceptance tests 3 and 6 of ADR 0021.

title: Stage 4C: reactions
description: ADR 0021 section 7. #Reaction has a rate and a tolerance, and its interactions have a ratio. native.rate computes the amount of the reaction once for a step. Acceptance test 4 of ADR 0021.

title: Stage 4D: transition conditions and overrides from C
description: ADR 0021 section 5, transition conditions. A map has a condition. The application can inspect, replace and clear it for an instance or for an exact type. A change takes effect at a boundary and the world records it for replay. Needs an amendment to ADR 0021 first: the syntax, named inputs, two true conditions, and the record. Acceptance test 5 of ADR 0021.
